question: the delivery gate had stood at accepted=false on a 3.24% beak-loss difference.  h, p and geometry order were each moved on the 24 mm fixture without shifting it.  Both routes sat below the infinite-length 2-D reference in the same order, so the remaining candidate was the fixture length
finding: doubling the fixture to 48 mm converges both routes onto the independent 2-D reference and closes the gate.  The beak loss fraction moves from -4.93% (BEM-A) and -1.88% (PEEC) of the reference to -0.24% and +0.34%; the pairwise difference falls from 3.21% to 0.58%.  Every acceptance metric then passes with at least five times margin, and the 48 mm run does it at fes_order=0, so the basis order was never what the fractions needed either
why_length: the fractions are ratios measured mid-span, and the source and sink caps carry an approximately length-independent loss -- 6.53, 6.76 and 6.90 micro-ohm at 6, 12 and 24 mm in the earlier sweep.  At 24 mm that end contribution is still large enough to depress the mid-span beak and tip shares of both routes, by different amounts because the two discretisations distribute the end current differently.  It is not a discretisation error in either, which is why no refinement control could reach it
not_claimed: this is a straight constant-section fin in copper at one frequency. It does not establish tapered or curved fins, brazed fin solids, filleted roots, nonlinear material, or the branch-current back-reaction of gate 4
